Vanessa — quick pass below with suggestions inline. I also attached a redline. High level: language is good, but we should avoid the phrase "we do not use data for training" without the DPA linkage — customers expect a clear exception for aggregated telemetry.

Inline notes (highlights):
- Retention: change to "We retain request and response content for up to 30 days for troubleshooting and abuse prevention, unless you configure data retention controls in the Console." (shorter, cites Console control)
- Subprocessors: add "View current subprocessors in our DPA (link). We require subprocessors to comply with the same protections as Redwood."
- Cross‑border: preferred to say "Requests may be routed across regions. We use encryption in transit and at rest and rely on standard contractual protections for transfers."

Attachment: hosted_privacy_snippets_v2_redlines.docx (redlines)

Alyssa — flagged a couple of items where Acme Legal may ask for a stronger transfer sentence (SCCs reference or similar).

Thanks for the ping — quick third‑party review below. Overall good direction: concise + actionable. My suggestions focus on two risks Acme Legal will probe: (1) transfer mechanisms and (2) subprocessors disclosure cadence.

Suggested short lines that are defensible and consumer‑friendly:
- Retention (one line): "We retain API request and response content for up to 30 days for troubleshooting and security; you can opt into shorter retention in Console settings."
- Training (one line): "We do not use your request or response content to train our public models unless you explicitly opt in in the Console."
- Subprocessors (one line): "We use subprocessors to operate the service; the current list and updates are published in the DPA and notifications are sent to customers with active agreements."
- Transfers (one line): "Requests may be routed across regions; transfers are governed by contractual safeguards (e.g., SCCs) and data is encrypted in transit and at rest."

Note: for the training sentence, add the qualifier "public models" to avoid implying no internal telemetry/aggregations — that'll help legal. Also recommend a single-line footer link: "See DPA / Subprocessors / Data Controls" pointing to the DPA and the Console page.

If you'd like, I can draft a single‑paragraph modal copy and a 2‑bullet footer.

Alyssa Ford
Principal Consultant, PrivacyConsult
